observations.note: The common X330 table and drawing explicitly list XL330-M077-T, XL330-M288-T, XC330-T288-T and XC330-M288-T with the same 20 x 34 x 26 mm envelope. This supports a shared nominal mechanical profile, not a shared electrical specification. Gear ratio for this named model is 77.5:1.

Chosen CAD axes rotate the manufacturer presentation: X follows manufacturer H (34 mm) from the shaft-near end; Y follows manufacturer W (20 mm); Z follows body depth 23 plus output projection 3. The manual lists overall 20 W x 34 H x 26 D mm. Physical production revision remains unknown.

Front/back frame assembly specifies M2 TAPPING screws. These must not be silently represented as already-machined ISO M2 threads. The separate optional idler assembly/cap uses a different M2.6 x 6 tapping screw and is not included in the base-profile model.

The manual links a common XL330/XC330 PDF at robotis.com/service/download.php?no=1986. That endpoint returned 404 during this audit, so numeric drawing facts here use the manufacturer-published common brochure rather than unreadable CAD files. The missing details remain unknown.

ROBOTIS distinguishes the separate HNX330 metal horn from the output shaft wheel gear, but that description does not establish the exact physical identity of the plastic-looking output face in this base preview. The original diameter 16 / projection 3 depiction remains a base-profile reference. A selected normal horn replaces the output-flange display role to avoid stacking two horn-like faces; this model policy is not a factory part-removal or packing claim.

assumptions: Main case 34 x 20 x 23 mm, front output diameter 16 mm, projection 3 mm and axis 9.5 mm from the short end use the manufacturer common X330 drawing. Curved corner and enclosure seam contours are simplified.

The 16 x 30 mm front/back corner pattern is registered symmetrically on the 20 x 34 mm nominal case using drawn centerlines. Independent edge-offset and manufacturing alignment tolerances are not provided by the brochure.

M2 is the documented TAPPING-screw nominal size, not a known tapped metric thread or pilot drill. The visible 1.6 mm short recesses are illustrative pilot geometry. Their depth, the output-face hole pattern and central recess are planning choices, not manufacturing instructions.
The rear idler ring is flush planning geometry at the documented coaxial position. Ring diameter 12, center opening 6 and recess depth 1 are approximate; no optional idler horn or cap is fitted.

There are two detachable TTL sockets with 3 contacts each. Amber shroud/cavity positions and sizes, as well as pin diameter and exposure, are approximate visual references. No connected plug, pigtail or cable is generated.

XL and XC share the common nominal mechanical drawing while ratios, motors and electrical ratings remain distinct. The base output-flange depiction is retained without asserting a precise factory plastic-part identity. Named accessory fit claims and replacement policy are separate horn-catalog records; angular phase and unverified seating remain explicit.
Colors distinguish roles and visual variants; they do not specify a production material finish or coating.

observations.note: The common X330 table and drawing explicitly list XL330-M077-T, XL330-M288-T, XC330-T288-T and XC330-M288-T with the same 20 x 34 x 26 mm envelope. This supports a shared nominal mechanical profile, not a shared electrical specification. Gear ratio for this named model is 288.35:1.

Chosen CAD axes rotate the manufacturer presentation: X follows manufacturer H (34 mm) from the shaft-near end; Y follows manufacturer W (20 mm); Z follows body depth 23 plus output projection 3. The manual lists overall 20 W x 34 H x 26 D mm. Physical production revision remains unknown.

Front/back frame assembly specifies M2 TAPPING screws. These must not be silently represented as already-machined ISO M2 threads. The separate optional idler assembly/cap uses a different M2.6 x 6 tapping screw and is not included in the base-profile model.

The manual links a common XL330/XC330 PDF at robotis.com/service/download.php?no=1986. That endpoint returned 404 during this audit, so numeric drawing facts here use the manufacturer-published common brochure rather than unreadable CAD files. The missing details remain unknown.

ROBOTIS distinguishes the separate HNX330 metal horn from the output shaft wheel gear, but that description does not establish the exact physical identity of the plastic-looking output face in this base preview. The original diameter 16 / projection 3 depiction remains a base-profile reference. A selected normal horn replaces the output-flange display role to avoid stacking two horn-like faces; this model policy is not a factory part-removal or packing claim.

assumptions: Main case 34 x 20 x 23 mm, front output diameter 16 mm, projection 3 mm and axis 9.5 mm from the short end use the manufacturer common X330 drawing. Curved corner and enclosure seam contours are simplified.

The 16 x 30 mm front/back corner pattern is registered symmetrically on the 20 x 34 mm nominal case using drawn centerlines. Independent edge-offset and manufacturing alignment tolerances are not provided by the brochure.

M2 is the documented TAPPING-screw nominal size, not a known tapped metric thread or pilot drill. The visible 1.6 mm short recesses are illustrative pilot geometry. Their depth, the output-face hole pattern and central recess are planning choices, not manufacturing instructions.
The rear idler ring is flush planning geometry at the documented coaxial position. Ring diameter 12, center opening 6 and recess depth 1 are approximate; no optional idler horn or cap is fitted.

There are two detachable TTL sockets with 3 contacts each. Amber shroud/cavity positions and sizes, as well as pin diameter and exposure, are approximate visual references. No connected plug, pigtail or cable is generated.

XL and XC share the common nominal mechanical drawing while ratios, motors and electrical ratings remain distinct. The base output-flange depiction is retained without asserting a precise factory plastic-part identity. Named accessory fit claims and replacement policy are separate horn-catalog records; angular phase and unverified seating remain explicit.
Colors distinguish roles and visual variants; they do not specify a production material finish or coating.
